_howTo: 1. Copy this file to workpacks/<seat>/interface.json. Look up your row in LY-006/registry/seats.json: writeZones, cutZones, ownsSourceObjects, ownsGroundPieces, ownsCuts, ownsCards, components, produces, consumes.
2. claims: list only objects the registry gives to YOUR seat (registry/ownership.json). Everything else is read-only; if you need it, set portsConsumed[].ack = rejected-needs-coordinator and stop.
3. zonesUsed: for each registry zoneId you write geometry into, give the AABBs (zone frame) of what you actually wrote; they must lie inside the zone box.

4. portsProduced: one record per registry port whose producer is your seat, same portId and version, measured local + world (world = frame placement * local; world stays null while the frame is unplaced) and measuredFrom with the file SHA256.
5. portsConsumed: every registry port you consume, same version, ack + measured residual against your geometry.
6. New ground pieces are named gp:<seat>:<name> and sit inside one of your write zones. Cuts in city ground are composed only by LY-090.
7. Moving parts stay separate nodes (never merged into static batches) and name the mount/opening port that carries their axis or state (hostPortId).

8. Run: python -I LY-006/source/validate_interface.py LY-006/registry <your interface.json> <your seat dir>. Changing any port value or version is a registry v2 request to LY-006 / the coordinator, never a local edit.
